problem: The trap says 'Do not call the feature vector the "pattern" when the exam asks for the pattern vector', which is self-contradictory and contradicts standard usage. In the standard textbooks the pattern vector and the feature vector are the same object: the ordered list of measurements x = (x₁, …, xₙ). A student following this trap could refuse to write x when asked for the pattern vector and lose marks.
fix: Replace with: 'A pattern is the set of measurements from one object, and the pattern vector (also called the feature vector) is those measurements written as an ordered list x = (x₁, …, xₙ). Do not confuse a pattern (one sample) with a pattern class (the set of samples sharing a property).'

problem: 'A feature is useful only if it separates the classes' is stated as a general rule and is too strong. A feature whose ranges overlap can still help when combined with another feature (two features that each overlap can jointly separate the classes). Only in the tomato example is area useless because R already separates perfectly.
fix: Say: 'A feature is useful if it helps separate the classes, alone or together with other features. In the tomato example area is dropped because R alone already separates the classes and the area ranges overlap.'
